atoms.shown: T_f = T₀ - i φ K_f b, b = w / (M_s (1 - w))

equation.name: How much salt lowers the freezing point
equation.formula:
b = w / (Ms * (1 - w))
T = T0 - i * phi * Kf * b

T0.name: freezing point of the pure solvent

source.text: Atkins, P. and de Paula, J. 2014, Atkins' Physical Chemistry, 10th edn, Oxford University Press

explain.curious: Salt water freezes colder than fresh water. A brine six times saltier than the sea stays liquid well below freezing, which is how oceans hide under ice.
explain.science: Freezing-point depression from the solute's molality, with the van 't Hoff factor and an osmotic coefficient for non-ideal brines. Good to about 10 percent up to 20 percent salt by mass; the NaCl eutectic (23 percent, 252 K) is the hard floor.

equation.name: Height of the waves a wind raises
equation.formula:
CD = cd0 * (c1 + c2 * U)
us = U * sqrt(CD)
q = us * us
x = g * X / q
Hs = min(aH * sqrt(x), bH) * q / g
Tp = min(aT * x ^ (1/3), bT) * us / g

U.name: wind speed ten metres above the water

X.name: stretch of open water the wind blows over

g.name: pull of gravity at the surface

cd0.name: scale of the sea's drag on the wind

aH.name: how fast wave height grows with fetch

bH.name: height of a fully grown sea

aT.name: how fast wave period grows with fetch

bT.name: period of a fully grown sea

Hs.name: significant wave height (the mean of the highest third)

source.text: US Army Corps of Engineers, Coastal Engineering Manual, EM 1110-2-1100, Part II, chapter 2
source.where: eqs. II-2-36 (fetch-limited growth), II-2-37 (fully developed limits) and the drag coefficient relation

explain.curious: Wind drags on the sea and builds waves; the longer the stretch of open water and the stronger the wind, the bigger they grow, until the sea is fully grown. Weaker gravity lets the same wind pile water higher, so Titan's seas would rise further for each breath of wind.
explain.science: Deep-water fetch-limited growth in friction-velocity scaling, g Hm0/u*² = 4.13×10⁻² (g X/u*²)^½ and g Tp/u* = 0.651 (g X/u*²)^⅓, capped at the fully developed 211.5 and 239.8, with u*² = C_D U10². Fitted on Earth: the ratio of air to liquid density and the liquid's viscosity and surface tension are Earth's (docs/fudges.md).
